content.text:
I fixed the bug in `src/Tokenizer.ts`, but I haven't run anything to confirm it. My attempt to test it with Node was blocked by the permission prompt, so neither your example nor the existing test suite has been run against the change.

**Cause:** links and images both go through the `outputLink` function. While it reads a link's text, it sets `lexer.state.inLink = true` so bare URLs and email addresses aren't turned into links. When it finished, it always set the flag back to `false`, even if it was still inside an outer link. So in `[![logo](logo.png) www.example.com](…)`, the image reset the flag partway through the outer link's text. The URL after it was then scanned as if it were outside any link and became a nested `<a>`.

**Fix:** `outputLink` now saves the previous `inLink` value before setting it to `true` and puts that value back afterwards (around lines 22–32). Outside any link, the flag still returns to `false` as before. Inside a link, it stays `true`, so the bare URL stays plain text.

Inline and reference-style links and images both use `outputLink`, and `https://` URLs and email addresses go through the same check, so this one change should cover every case in the report. No other behaviour should change.

To check it, run the existing test suite and render your example once dependencies are installed.
